background: Lloyds Banking Group is the holding company of the UK's largest retail and commercial bank, owner of Lloyds Bank, Halifax, Bank of Scotland and Scottish Widows, with almost all of its business in Britain.
synthesis: Two of the three main agencies rate the group, A on average, the weakest of them at A-, both on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 10 Sep 2025. Capital is mixed against UK majors, leverage of 5.1% in the top quarter but CET1 of 13.6% just below the peer median, and liquidity likewise, LCR of 144% above the median and NSFR of 123% below it. Since 30 Jun 2025 leverage has fallen 0.3 points while CET1, LCR and NSFR have been broadly flat (figures to 30 Jun 2026). The newest flagged item, on 2 Oct 2026, is an online banking outage across its brands, with the £1.2bn Arena Television fraud claims before it.
